celaleyn:91-91.t: ﴿وَ﴾ and mention Maryam, ﴿الَّتِي أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا﴾ she guarded it from being touched, ﴿فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ رُوحِنَا﴾ i.e. Jibrīl, when he blew into the opening of the neck of her shift, so she conceived ʿĪsā, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهَا وَابْنَهَا آيَةً لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ humans, jinn and angels, since she bore him without a male.

celaleyn:92-92.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذِهِ﴾ i.e. the religion of Islam ﴿أُمَّتُكُمْ﴾ is your religion, O you who are addressed, i.e. you must hold to it, ﴿أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ a permanent ḥāl (circumstantial), ﴿وَأَنَا رَبُّكُمْ فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ affirm My oneness.

celaleyn:93-93.t: ﴿وَتَقَطَّعُوا﴾ i.e. some of those addressed ﴿أَمْرَهُمْ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ i.e. they split up the affair of their religion, differing over it; they are the sects of the Jews and the Christians. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿كُلٌّ إِلَيْنَا رَاجِعُونَ﴾ i.e. and We shall recompense each for his deeds.

celaleyn:94-94.t: ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِنَ الصَّالِحَاتِ وَهُوَ مُؤْمِنٌ فَلَا كُفْرَانَ﴾ i.e. no denial ﴿لِسَعْيِهِ وَإِنَّا لَهُ كَاتِبُونَ﴾ in that We command the recording angels to write it down, and We shall recompense him for it.

celaleyn:95-95.t: ﴿وَحَرَامٌ عَلَى قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا﴾ its people are meant ﴿أَنَّهُمْ لَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida) ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ i.e. their return to this world is impossible.

celaleyn:96-96.t: ﴿حَتَّى﴾ marks the limit of the impossibility of their return ﴿إِذَا فُتِحَتْ﴾ read without and with doubling [of the tāʾ] ﴿يَأْجُوجُ وَمَأْجُوجُ﴾ with the hamza and without it; two foreign names of two tribes, and a muḍāf is implied before it, i.e. their barrier; and that is near the Resurrection, ﴿وَهُمْ مِنْ كُلِّ حَدَبٍ﴾ raised ground ﴿يَنْسِلُونَ﴾ they hasten.

celaleyn:97-97.t: ﴿وَاقْتَرَبَ الْوَعْدُ الْحَقُّ﴾ i.e. the Day of Resurrection, ﴿فَإِذَا هِيَ﴾ i.e. the matter [al-qiṣṣa] ﴿شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ on that Day because of its severity; they say: ﴿يَا﴾ for calling attention ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ our ruin! ﴿قَدْ كُنَّا﴾ in the world ﴿فِي غَفْلَةٍ مِنْ هَذَا﴾ Day; ﴿بَلْ كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ to ourselves, by our denying the messengers.

celaleyn:98-98.t: ﴿إِنَّكُمْ﴾ O people of Mecca ﴿وَمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. other than Him, of the idols, ﴿حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ are its fuel; ﴿أَنْتُمْ لَهَا وَارِدُونَ﴾ entering it.

celaleyn:99-99.t: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ idols ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ as you claim, ﴿مَا وَرَدُوهَا﴾ they would not have entered it; ﴿وَكُلٌّ﴾ of the worshippers and the worshipped ﴿فِيهَا خَالِدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:100-100.t: ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ for the worshippers ﴿فِيهَا زَفِيرٌ وَهُمْ فِيهَا لَا يَسْمَعُونَ﴾ anything, because of the intensity of its boiling. And [the following] was revealed when Ibn al-Zibaʿrā said: ʿUzayr, the Messiah and the angels have been worshipped, so they are in the Fire according to what preceded.

celaleyn:101-101.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا﴾ the rank ﴿الْحُسْنَى﴾ and among them are those mentioned, ﴿أُولَئِكَ عَنْهَا مُبْعَدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:102-102.t: ﴿لَا يَسْمَعُونَ حَسِيسَهَا﴾ its sound, ﴿وَهُمْ فِي مَا اشْتَهَتْ أَنْفُسُهُمْ﴾ of bliss ﴿خَالِدُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:103-103.t: ﴿لَا يَحْزُنُهُمُ الْفَزَعُ الْأَكْبَرُ﴾ which is when the servant is ordered off to the Fire, ﴿وَتَتَلَقَّاهُمْ﴾ receives them ﴿الْمَلَائِكَةُ﴾ when they come out of the graves, saying to them: ﴿هَذَا يَوْمُكُمُ الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ تُوعَدُونَ﴾ in the world.

celaleyn:104-104.t: ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ accusative (manṣūb) by «اذكر» (mention) implied (muqaddar) before it ﴿نَطْوِي السَّمَاءَ كَطَيِّ السِّجِلِّ﴾ the name of an angel ﴿لِلْكِتَابِ﴾ the scroll of the son of Adam at his death, and the lām is redundant (zāʾida); or al-sijill is the scroll and al-kitāb is in the sense of «مكتوب» (what is written), and the lām is in the sense of «على». In one reading [لِلْكُتُبِ] as a plural. ﴿كَمَا بَدَأْنَا أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍ﴾ from nothing ﴿نُعِيدُهُ﴾ after annihilating it; so the kāf is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نعيد», its pronoun refers back to «أول», and «ما» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun). ﴿وَعْدًا عَلَيْنَا﴾ accusative by «وعدنا» implied before it, and it emphasises the content of what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾ what We have promised.

celaleyn:105-105.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِي الزَّبُورِ﴾ in the sense of «الكتاب», i.e. the revealed books of Allah, ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِ الذِّكْرِ﴾ in the sense of the Mother of the Book which is with Allah, ﴿أَنَّ الْأَرْضَ﴾ the land of the Garden ﴿يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِيَ الصَّالِحُونَ﴾ general, covering every righteous person.

celaleyn:106-106.t: ﴿إِنَّ فِي هَذَا﴾ Qurʾān ﴿لَبَلَاغًا﴾ sufficiency for entering the Garden ﴿لِقَوْمٍ عَابِدِينَ﴾ who act by it.

celaleyn:107-107.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ﴾ O Muhammad ﴿إِلَّا رَحْمَةً﴾ i.e. for mercy ﴿لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ humans and jinn, through you.

celaleyn:108-108.t: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّمَا يُوحَى إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ﴾ i.e. nothing is revealed to me concerning the God except His oneness. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ﴾ submitting to what is revealed to me of the oneness of the God? The question is in the sense of a command.

celaleyn:109-109.t: ﴿فَإِنْ تَوَلَّوْا﴾ from that, ﴿فَقُلْ آذَنْتُكُمْ﴾ of war ﴿عَلَى سَوَاءٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from both the fāʿil (agent) and the mafʿūl (object), i.e. equal in knowledge of it; I do not keep it to myself apart from you, so that you may make ready. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ أَمْ بَعِيدٌ مَا تُوعَدُونَ﴾ of punishment, or the Resurrection which includes it; only Allah knows it.

celaleyn:110-110.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ the Exalted ﴿يَعْلَمُ الْجَهْرَ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ﴾ and deed, from you and from others, ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا تَكْتُمُونَ﴾ you and others, of what is secret.

celaleyn:111-111.t: ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ not ﴿أَدْرِي لَعَلَّهُ﴾ i.e. what I have informed you of, whose time is not known, ﴿فِتْنَةٌ﴾ a test ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ so that He may see how you act, ﴿وَمَتَاعٌ﴾ enjoyment ﴿إِلَى حِينٍ﴾ i.e. the ending of your lifespans. This is set against the first, which is hoped for with «لعل»; the second is not a place for hoping.

celaleyn:112-112.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ and in one reading [قَالَ] ﴿رَبِّ احْكُمْ﴾ between me and those who deny me ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ with punishment for them or victory over them; so they were punished at Badr, Uḥud, al-Aḥzāb, Ḥunayn and al-Khandaq, and he was given victory over them. ﴿وَرَبُّنَا الرَّحْمَنُ الْمُسْتَعَانُ عَلَى مَا تَصِفُونَ﴾ of your lying against Allah in your saying "He has taken a son", and against me in your saying "a sorcerer", and against the Qurʾān in your saying "poetry". [Translator's note: al-Aḥzāb and al-Khandaq are usually names of the same battle; the source lists them separately.]

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿اقْتَرَبَ﴾ — has drawn near — ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ — the people of Mecca, deniers of the resurrection — ﴿حِسَابُهُمْ﴾ — on the Day of Resurrection — ﴿وَهُمْ فِي غَفْلَةٍ﴾ — about it — ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — from preparing for it through faith.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِمْ مُحْدَثٍ﴾ — little by little, i.e. the wording of the Quran — ﴿إِلَّا اسْتَمَعُوهُ وَهُمْ يَلْعَبُونَ﴾ — mocking,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿لَاهِيَةً﴾ — heedless — ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ﴾ — of its meaning. ﴿وَأَسَرُّوا النَّجْوَى﴾ — i.e. the talk — ﴿الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا﴾ — a badal (substitute) from the wāw of "wa-asarrū al-najwā": ﴿هَلْ هَذَا﴾ — i.e. Muḥammad — ﴿إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ﴾ — so what he brings is sorcery? ﴿أَفَتَأْتُونَ السِّحْرَ﴾ — follow it — ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ — knowing that it is sorcery?

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — to them — ﴿رَبِّي يَعْلَمُ الْقَوْلَ﴾ — being — ﴿فِي السَّمَاءِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ﴾ — of what they kept secret — ﴿الْعَلِيمُ﴾ — of it.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ — for transition from one purpose to another, in the three places — ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — about the Quran he brought: it is — ﴿أَضْغَاثُ أَحْلَامٍ﴾ — jumbles he saw in sleep — ﴿بَلِ افْتَرَاهُ﴾ — fabricated it — ﴿بَلْ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ﴾ — so what he brought is poetry. ﴿فَلْيَأْتِنَا بِآيَةٍ كَمَا أُرْسِلَ الْأَوَّلُونَ﴾ — such as the she-camel, the staff and the hand. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿مَا آمَنَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ — i.e. its people — ﴿أَهْلَكْنَاهَا﴾ — for denying the signs that came to it. ﴿أَفَهُمْ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — No.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا قَبْلَكَ إِلَّا رِجَالًا يُوحَى﴾ — and in one reading [نُوحِي], with nūn and kasra on the ḥāʾ — ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ — not angels. ﴿فَاسْأَلُوا أَهْلَ الذِّكْرِ﴾ — those learned in the Torah and the Gospel — ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ لَا تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ — that, for they know it, and you are closer to believing them than to believing the believers in Muḥammad.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَاهُمْ﴾ — the messengers — ﴿جَسَدًا﴾ — meaning bodies — ﴿لَا يَأْكُلُونَ الطَّعَامَ﴾ — rather they eat it — ﴿وَمَا كَانُوا خَالِدِينَ﴾ — in the world.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ صَدَقْنَاهُمُ الْوَعْدَ﴾ — of saving them — ﴿فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُمْ وَمَنْ نَشَاءُ﴾ — i.e. those who believed them — ﴿وَأَهْلَكْنَا الْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾ — those who denied them.

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿لَقَدْ أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ﴾ — O company of Quraysh — ﴿كِتَابًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ﴾ — because it is in your language. ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ — and so believe in it?

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَكَمْ قَصَمْنَا﴾ — We destroyed — ﴿مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ﴾ — i.e. its people — ﴿كَانَتْ ظَالِمَةً﴾ — disbelieving — ﴿وَأَنْشَأْنَا بَعْدَهَا قَوْمًا آخَرِينَ﴾

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَحَسُّوا بَأْسَنَا﴾ — i.e. the people of the town sensed the destruction — ﴿إِذَا هُمْ مِنْهَا يَرْكُضُونَ﴾ — fleeing in haste. So the angels said to them mockingly:

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿لَا تَرْكُضُوا وَارْجِعُوا إِلَى مَا أُتْرِفْتُمْ﴾ — you were given luxury — ﴿فِيهِ وَمَسَاكِنِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُسْأَلُونَ﴾ — for something of your worldly goods, as usual.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَالُوا يَا﴾ — for calling attention (li-l-tanbīh) — ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ — our destruction! ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ — through disbelief.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿فَمَا زَالَتْ تِلْكَ﴾ — words — ﴿دَعْوَاهُمْ﴾ — they called out with them and repeated them — ﴿حَتَّى جَعَلْنَاهُمْ حَصِيدًا﴾ — i.e. like crops reaped with sickles, by their being killed with the sword — ﴿خَامِدِينَ﴾ — dead, like the dying down of fire when it is extinguished.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَاعِبِينَ﴾ — in idle play, but rather as pointing to Our power and benefiting Our servants.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿لَوْ أَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَتَّخِذَ لَهْوًا﴾ — something to divert oneself with, such as a wife or a child — ﴿لَاتَّخَذْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا﴾ — from Our presence, from the wide-eyed houris and the angels — ﴿إِنْ كُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾ — that; but We did not do it, so We did not will it.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿بَلْ نَقْذِفُ﴾ — We hurl — ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — faith — ﴿عَلَى الْبَاطِلِ﴾ — disbelief — ﴿فَيَدْمَغُهُ﴾ — removes it — ﴿فَإِذَا هُوَ زَاهِقٌ﴾ — vanishing. Damaghahu originally means "struck his brain (dimāgh)", which is a fatal spot. ﴿وَلَكُمْ﴾ — O disbelievers of Mecca — ﴿الْوَيْلُ﴾ — severe punishment — ﴿مِمَّا تَصِفُونَ﴾ — Allah with, of a wife or a child.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَلَهُ﴾ — the Exalted — ﴿مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ — as possession. ﴿وَمَنْ عِنْدَهُ﴾ — i.e. the angels; a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is ﴿لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ عَنْ عِبَادَتِهِ وَلَا يَسْتَحْسِرُونَ﴾ — they do not grow weary.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ لَا يَفْتُرُونَ﴾ — from it; for it is to them like breathing is to us: nothing distracts us from it.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ — meaning "bal" (rather), for transition, and the hamza for disapproval (inkār) — ﴿اتَّخَذُوا آلِهَةً﴾ — being — ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ — such as stone, gold and silver — ﴿هُمْ﴾ — i.e. the gods — ﴿يُنْشِرُونَ﴾ — i.e. bring the dead to life? No; and none is a god except one who brings the dead to life.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿لَوْ كَانَ فِيهِمَا﴾ — i.e. the heavens and the earth — ﴿آلِهَةٌ إِلَّا اللَّهُ﴾ — i.e. other than Him — ﴿لَفَسَدَتَا﴾ — they would have departed from their observed order, because of the mutual obstruction among them, in accordance with what usually happens when there are several rulers: mutual obstruction in a matter and lack of agreement on it. ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ﴾ — exalted above all is — ﴿اللَّهِ رَبِّ﴾ — the Creator of — ﴿الْعَرْشِ﴾ — the Throne (al-kursī) — ﴿عَمَّا يَصِفُونَ﴾ — the disbelievers, Allah with, of a partner to Him and other things.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿لَا يُسْأَلُ عَمَّا يَفْعَلُ وَهُمْ يُسْأَلُونَ﴾ — about their deeds.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ — the Exalted, i.e. besides Him — ﴿آلِهَةً﴾ — in it is an interrogative of rebuke (istifhām tawbīkh). ﴿قُلْ هَاتُوا بُرْهَانَكُمْ﴾ — for that; and there is no way to it. ﴿هَذَا ذِكْرُ مَنْ مَعِيَ﴾ — i.e. my community, and it is the Quran — ﴿وَذِكْرُ مَنْ قَبْلِي﴾ — of the nations, and it is the Torah, the Gospel and others of the books of Allah; in none of them is it [stated] that there is a god with Allah of the kind they claimed — He is exalted above that. ﴿بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ الْحَقَّ﴾ — i.e. the oneness of Allah — ﴿فَهُمْ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — from the reflection that leads to it.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا يُوحَى﴾ — and in one reading [نُوحِي], with nūn and kasra on the ḥāʾ — ﴿إِلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنَا فَاعْبُدُونِ﴾ — i.e. affirm My oneness.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا اتَّخَذَ الرَّحْمَنُ وَلَدًا﴾ — from among the angels. ﴿سُبْحَانَهُ بَلْ﴾ — they are — ﴿عِبَادٌ مُكْرَمُونَ﴾ — with Him; and servitude is incompatible with being begotten.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿لَا يَسْبِقُونَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ — they do not utter their speech except after His speech — ﴿وَهُمْ بِأَمْرِهِ يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ — i.e. after it.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ﴾ — i.e. what they have done and what they will do — ﴿وَلَا يَشْفَعُونَ إِلَّا لِمَنِ ارْتَضَى﴾ — the Exalted, that intercession be made for him — ﴿وَهُمْ مِنْ خَشْيَتِهِ﴾ — the Exalted — ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ — fearful.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يَقُلْ مِنْهُمْ إِنِّي إِلَهٌ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾ — i.e. Allah, i.e. other than Him; and he is Iblīs, who called to the worship of himself and commanded obedience to himself — ﴿فَذَلِكَ نَجْزِيهِ جَهَنَّمَ كَذَلِكَ﴾ — just as We requite him — ﴿نَجْزِي الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — i.e. the idolaters.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿أَوَلَمْ﴾ — with wāw and without it — ﴿يَرَ﴾ — know — ﴿الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ كَانَتَا رَتْقًا﴾ — i.e. a closed mass, meaning closed up — ﴿فَفَتَقْنَاهُمَا﴾ — We made the heaven seven and the earth seven; or the opening of the heaven, in that it used not to rain and then it rained, and the opening of the earth, in that it used not to grow plants and then it grew them. ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِنَ الْمَاءِ﴾ — which descends from the sky and springs from the earth — ﴿كُلَّ شَيْءٍ حَيٍّ﴾ — of plants and other things; i.e. water is a cause of its life. ﴿أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ — in My oneness?

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رَوَاسِيَ﴾ — firm mountains — so that ﴿أَنْ﴾ — not — ﴿تَمِيدَ﴾ — move — ﴿بِهِمْ وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا﴾ — i.e. the mountains — ﴿فِجَاجًا﴾ — passages — ﴿سُبُلًا﴾ — a badal (substitute), i.e. wide through-roads — ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ﴾ — to their destinations on journeys.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا السَّمَاءَ سَقْفًا﴾ — for the earth, like the roof of a house — ﴿مَحْفُوظًا﴾ — from falling. ﴿وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا﴾ — the sun, the moon and the stars — ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — they do not reflect on them so as to know that their Creator has no partner.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ وَالشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ﴾ — its tanwīn is a replacement for the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct): of the sun and the moon and what follows them, namely the stars — ﴿فِي فَلَكٍ﴾ — i.e. a circular one, like a millstone, in the sky — ﴿يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ — move swiftly, like one swimming in water; and because of the comparison with him, He used the pronoun of the plural of rational beings. And the following was revealed when the disbelievers said, "Muḥammad will die":

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا لِبَشَرٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ الْخُلْدَ﴾ — i.e. remaining forever in the world. ﴿أَفَإِنْ مِتَّ فَهُمُ الْخَالِدُونَ﴾ — in it? No. So the last clause is the locus of the interrogative of disapproval (al-istifhām al-inkārī).

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ذَائِقَةُ الْمَوْتِ﴾ — in the world. ﴿وَنَبْلُوكُمْ﴾ — We test you — ﴿بِالشَّرِّ وَالْخَيْرِ﴾ — such as poverty and wealth, sickness and health — ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ — a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. so that We may see whether you will be patient and grateful or not. ﴿وَإِلَيْنَا تُرْجَعُونَ﴾ — and We will requite you.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿وَإِذَا رَآكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِنْ﴾ — "not" — ﴿يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا﴾ — i.e. an object of mockery, saying: ﴿أَهَذَا الَّذِي يَذْكُرُ آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ — i.e. finds fault with them? ﴿وَهُمْ بِذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — to them — ﴿هُمْ﴾ — a tawkīd (emphasis) — ﴿كَافِرُونَ﴾ — of it, since they said, "We do not know him." And the following was revealed about their seeking to hasten the punishment:

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿خُلِقَ الْإِنْسَانُ مِنْ عَجَلٍ﴾ — i.e. because of his great haste in his affairs, it is as if he were created from it. ﴿سَأُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِي﴾ — My promises of punishment — ﴿فَلَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونِ﴾ — about it. So He showed them killing at Badr.

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ مَتَى هَذَا الْوَعْدُ﴾ — of the Resurrection — ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ — in it? The Exalted said:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿لَوْ يَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا حِينَ لَا يَكُفُّونَ﴾ — ward off — ﴿عَنْ وُجُوهِهِمُ النَّارَ وَلَا عَنْ ظُهُورِهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ — protected from it at the Resurrection; and the jawāb (apodosis) of "law" is: they would not have said that.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿بَلْ تَأْتِيهِمْ﴾ — the Resurrection — ﴿بَغْتَةً فَتَبْهَتُهُمْ﴾ — bewilders them — ﴿فَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ رَدَّهَا وَلَا هُمْ يُنْظَرُونَ﴾ — given respite for repentance or excuse.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَلَقَدِ اسْتُهْزِئَ بِرُسُلٍ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ — in it is consolation for the Prophet ﷺ — ﴿فَحَاقَ﴾ — descended — ﴿بِالَّذِينَ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُمْ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾ — and it is the punishment; so likewise it will descend upon whoever mocks you.

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿مَنْ يَكْلَؤُكُمْ﴾ — protects you — ﴿بِاللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — from His punishment, if it descends upon you? I.e. no one does that. And those addressed do not fear Allah's punishment because they deny it. ﴿بَلْ هُمْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ — they do not reflect on it.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿أَمْ﴾ — in it is the meaning of the hamza, for disapproval, i.e. "a-" — ﴿لَهُمْ آلِهَةٌ تَمْنَعُهُمْ﴾ — from what would harm them — ﴿مِنْ دُونِنَا﴾ — i.e. do they have anyone other than Us who protects them from it? ﴿لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾ — i.e. the gods — ﴿نَصْرَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ — so they will not help them — ﴿وَلَا هُمْ﴾ — i.e. the disbelievers — ﴿مِنَّا﴾ — from Our punishment — ﴿يُصْحَبُونَ﴾ — given protection; one says "ṣaḥibaka Allāh", i.e. may He guard you and protect you.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿بَلْ مَتَّعْنَا هَؤُلَاءِ وَآبَاءَهُمْ﴾ — with what We bestowed on them — ﴿حَتَّى طَالَ عَلَيْهِمُ الْعُمُرُ﴾ — and they were deluded by that. ﴿أَفَلَا يَرَوْنَ أَنَّا نَأْتِي الْأَرْضَ﴾ — We aim at their land — ﴿نَنْقُصُهَا مِنْ أَطْرَافِهَا﴾ — by conquest for the Prophet? ﴿أَفَهُمُ الْغَالِبُونَ﴾ — No; rather the Prophet and his Companions.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ — to them — ﴿إِنَّمَا أُنْذِرُكُمْ بِالْوَحْيِ﴾ — from Allah, not from myself. ﴿وَلَا يَسْمَعُ الصُّمُّ الدُّعَاءَ إِذَا﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second lightened (tashīl) between it and yāʾ — ﴿مَا يُنْذَرُونَ﴾ — i.e. they, because they abandon acting upon the warning they have heard, are like the deaf.

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ مَسَّتْهُمْ نَفْحَةٌ﴾ — a light blow — ﴿مِنْ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَا﴾ — for calling attention (li-l-tanbīh) — ﴿وَيْلَنَا﴾ — our destruction! ﴿إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَالِمِينَ﴾ — through associating partners and denying Muḥammad.

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَنَضَعُ الْمَوَازِينَ الْقِسْطَ﴾ — possessing justice — ﴿لِيَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ — i.e. on it — ﴿فَلَا تُظْلَمُ نَفْسٌ شَيْئًا﴾ — by the reduction of a good deed or the addition of a bad deed. ﴿وَإِنْ كَانَ﴾ — the deed — ﴿مِثْقَالَ﴾ — the weight of — ﴿حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ أَتَيْنَا بِهَا﴾ — with what is to be weighed of it. ﴿وَكَفَى بِنَا حَاسِبِينَ﴾ — reckoning everything precisely.

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى وَهَارُونَ الْفُرْقَانَ﴾ — i.e. the Torah, which distinguishes between truth and falsehood, the lawful and the unlawful — ﴿وَضِيَاءً﴾ — through it — ﴿وَذِكْرًا﴾ — i.e. an admonition through it — ﴿لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَيْبِ﴾ — out of sight of people, i.e. in private away from them — ﴿وَهُمْ مِنَ السَّاعَةِ﴾ — i.e. its terrors — ﴿مُشْفِقُونَ﴾ — i.e. fearful.

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿وَهَذَا﴾ — i.e. the Quran — ﴿ذِكْرٌ مُبَارَكٌ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ أَفَأَنْتُمْ لَهُ مُنْكِرُونَ﴾ — the interrogative in it is for rebuke (tawbīkh).

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ رُشْدَهُ مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. his guidance, before he reached maturity — ﴿وَكُنَّا بِهِ عَالِمِينَ﴾ — i.e. that he was worthy of that.

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا هَذِهِ التَّمَاثِيلُ﴾ — the idols — ﴿الَّتِي أَنْتُمْ لَهَا عَاكِفُونَ﴾ — i.e. persisting in worshipping them?

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿قَالُوا وَجَدْنَا آبَاءَنَا لَهَا عَابِدِينَ﴾ — so we followed their example.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — to them — ﴿لَقَدْ كُنْتُمْ أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمْ﴾ — by worshipping them — ﴿فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ — clear.

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿قَالُوا أَجِئْتَنَا بِالْحَقِّ﴾ — in this saying of yours — ﴿أَمْ أَنْتَ مِنَ اللَّاعِبِينَ﴾ — in it?

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿قَالَ بَلْ رَبُّكُمْ﴾ — who is deserving of worship — ﴿رَبُّ﴾ — is the Owner of — ﴿السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ الَّذِي فَطَرَهُنَّ﴾ — created them without any previous model — ﴿وَأَنَا عَلَى ذَلِكُمْ﴾ — which I have said — ﴿مِنَ الشَّاهِدِينَ﴾ — to it.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿وَتَاللَّهِ لَأَكِيدَنَّ أَصْنَامَكُمْ بَعْدَ أَنْ تُوَلُّوا مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُمْ﴾ — after they had gone to their gathering on a feast day of theirs — ﴿جُذَاذًا﴾ — with ḍamma on the jīm and with kasra on it; fragments, with an axe — ﴿إِلَّا كَبِيرًا لَهُمْ﴾ — he hung the axe on its neck — ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِ﴾ — i.e. to the big one — ﴿يَرْجِعُونَ﴾ — and see what it did to the others.

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — after their return and their seeing what had been done — ﴿مَنْ فَعَلَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا إِنَّهُ لَمِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — in it.

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — i.e. some of them to others — ﴿سَمِعْنَا فَتًى يَذْكُرُهُمْ﴾ — i.e. finding fault with them — ﴿يُقَالُ لَهُ إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿قَالُوا فَأْتُوا بِهِ عَلَى أَعْيُنِ النَّاسِ﴾ — i.e. openly — ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْهَدُونَ﴾ — against him, that he is the one who did it.

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ — to him, after he was brought — ﴿أَأَنْتَ﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, with the second changed into an alif, and with it lightened (tashīl), and with an alif inserted between the lightened one and the other, and without it — ﴿فَعَلْتَ هَذَا بِآلِهَتِنَا يَا إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿قَالَ﴾ — keeping silent about his own deed — ﴿بَلْ فَعَلَهُ كَبِيرُهُمْ هَذَا فَاسْأَلُوهُمْ﴾ — about who did it — ﴿إِنْ كَانُوا يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ — in it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) placed first; and in what precedes it is an allusion to them that an idol known to be incapable of acting cannot be a god.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿فَرَجَعُوا إِلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ — through reflection — ﴿فَقَالُوا﴾ — to themselves — ﴿إِنَّكُمْ أَنْتُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ — i.e. by your worshipping what does not speak.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿ثُمَّ نُكِسُوا﴾ — by Allah — ﴿عَلَى رُءُوسِهِمْ﴾ — i.e. they were returned to their disbelief, and they said: by Allah, ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ﴾ — i.e. so how can you order us to ask them?

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿قَالَ أَفَتَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ — i.e. instead of Him — ﴿مَا لَا يَنْفَعُكُمْ شَيْئًا﴾ — of provision and other things — ﴿وَلَا يَضُرُّكُمْ﴾ — in anything, if you do not worship it?

celaleyn:67-67.t: ﴿أُفٍّ﴾ — with kasra on the fāʾ and with fatḥa on it; in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. stench and ugliness — ﴿لَكُمْ وَلِمَا تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ — i.e. other than Him. ﴿أَفَلَا تَعْقِلُونَ﴾ — that these idols do not deserve worship and are not fit for it, and that only Allah the Exalted deserves it?

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿قَالُوا حَرِّقُوهُ﴾ — i.e. Ibrāhīm — ﴿وَانْصُرُوا آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ — i.e. by burning him — ﴿إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فَاعِلِينَ﴾ — helping them. So they gathered a great deal of firewood for him and set all of it ablaze, and they bound Ibrāhīm, put him in a catapult and threw him into the fire. The Exalted said:

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿قُلْنَا يَا نَارُ كُونِي بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ﴾ — so it burned nothing of him except his bonds; its heat went away and its light remained. And by His saying {وَسَلَامًا} he was kept safe from dying of its coldness.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿وَأَرَادُوا بِهِ كَيْدًا﴾ — and that was the burning — ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُمُ الْأَخْسَرِينَ﴾ — in what they intended.

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَلُوطًا﴾ — the son of his brother Hārān — from Iraq ﴿إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ — with abundant rivers and trees; and it is Syria (al-Shām). Ibrāhīm settled in Palestine and Lūṭ in al-Muʾtafika, and between them is a day's [journey].

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ — i.e. to Ibrāhīm; and he had asked for a child, as mentioned in al-Ṣāffāt — ﴿إِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ نَافِلَةً﴾ — i.e. in addition to what was asked for; or it is the child's child — ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ — i.e. him and his two sons — ﴿جَعَلْنَا صَالِحِينَ﴾ — prophets.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ أَئِمَّةً﴾ — with both hamzas pronounced fully, and with the second changed into a yāʾ; who are followed in good — ﴿يَهْدُونَ﴾ — people — ﴿بِأَمْرِنَا﴾ — to Our religion — ﴿وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْهِمْ فِعْلَ الْخَيْرَاتِ وَإِقَامَ الصَّلَوةِ وَإِيتَاءَ الزَّكَوةِ﴾ — i.e. that they be done, established and given, by them and by their followers; and the dropping of the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa) of "iqāma" is for lightness — ﴿وَكَانُوا لَنَا عَابِدِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿وَلُوطًا آتَيْنَاهُ حُكْمًا﴾ — judgement between disputants — ﴿وَعِلْمًا وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي كَانَتْ تَعْمَلُ﴾ — i.e. its people, the deeds — ﴿الْخَبَائِثَ﴾ — of sodomy, shooting with pellets, playing with birds and other than that. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ﴾ — the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "sāʾahu" (it grieved him), the opposite of "sarrahu" (it pleased him) — ﴿فَاسِقِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُ فِي رَحْمَتِنَا﴾ — in that We saved him from his people. ﴿إِنَّهُ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿نُوحًا﴾ — and what follows is a badal (substitute) from it — ﴿إِذْ نَادَى﴾ — invoked against his people with his saying {رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْ}, etc. — ﴿مِنْ قَبْلُ﴾ — i.e. before Ibrāhīm and Lūṭ — ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ﴾ — who were in his ark — ﴿مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ﴾ — i.e. drowning, and his people's denial of him.

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿وَنَصَرْنَاهُ﴾ — We protected him — ﴿مِنَ الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا﴾ — which prove his messengership — so that they could not reach him with harm. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ كَانُوا قَوْمَ سَوْءٍ فَأَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿دَاوُدَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾ — i.e. their story; and there is substituted (badal) from them — ﴿إِذْ يَحْكُمَانِ فِي الْحَرْثِ﴾ — it was crops or a vineyard — ﴿إِذْ نَفَشَتْ فِيهِ غَنَمُ الْقَوْمِ﴾ — i.e. grazed in it at night without a shepherd, having got loose — ﴿وَكُنَّا لِحُكْمِهِمْ شَاهِدِينَ﴾ — in it is the use of the plural pronoun for two. Dāwūd said: the owner of the field gets the sheep themselves. Sulaymān said: he benefits from their milk, offspring and wool until the field returns to what it was, through its [the sheep's] owner restoring it, and then he returns them to him.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿فَفَهَّمْنَاهَا﴾ — i.e. the judgement — ﴿سُلَيْمَانَ﴾ — and the judgement of both was by ijtihād (independent reasoning), and Dāwūd deferred to Sulaymān; and it is said it was by revelation, the second abrogating the first. ﴿وَكُلًّا﴾ — of the two — ﴿آتَيْنَا﴾ — him — ﴿حُكْمًا﴾ — prophethood — ﴿وَعِلْمًا﴾ — of the matters of religion. ﴿وَسَخَّرْنَا مَعَ دَاوُدَ الْجِبَالَ يُسَبِّحْنَ وَالطَّيْرَ﴾ — likewise; both were made subject to glorify with him, at his command, whenever he felt slackness, so that he would be invigorated for it. ﴿وَكُنَّا فَاعِلِينَ﴾ — the subjecting of them to glorify with him, even if it is a wonder to you, i.e. their answering the master Dāwūd.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ صَنْعَةَ لَبُوسٍ﴾ — and it is the coat of mail, because it is worn (tulbas); he was the first to make it, and before it there were plates — ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ — among all people — ﴿لِنُحْصِنَكُمْ﴾ — with nūn, referring to Allah; with the lower-dotted letter (yāʾ), referring to Dāwūd; and with the upper-dotted letter (tāʾ) [لِتُحْصِنَكُمْ], referring to the mail — ﴿مِنْ بَأْسِكُمْ﴾ — your war with your enemies. ﴿فَهَلْ أَنْتُمْ﴾ — O people of Mecca — ﴿شَاكِرُونَ﴾ — My blessings, by believing the Messenger? I.e. thank Me by that.

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — We subjected — ﴿لِسُلَيْمَانَ الرِّيحَ عَاصِفَةً﴾ — and in another verse "rukhāʾan" (gently), i.e. blowing strongly or lightly according to his will — ﴿تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ إِلَى الْأَرْضِ الَّتِي بَارَكْنَا فِيهَا﴾ — and it is Syria (al-Shām). ﴿وَكُنَّا بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَالِمِينَ﴾ — among that is His knowledge, the Exalted, that what He gives Sulaymān calls him to humility before his Lord; so His action, the Exalted, is in accordance with what His knowledge requires.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — We subjected — ﴿مِنَ الشَّيَاطِينِ مَنْ يَغُوصُونَ لَهُ﴾ — they enter the sea and bring out jewels from it for Sulaymān — ﴿وَيَعْمَلُونَ عَمَلًا دُونَ ذَلِكَ﴾ — i.e. other than diving, such as building and other things — ﴿وَكُنَّا لَهُمْ حَافِظِينَ﴾ — from spoiling what they had made, because whenever they finished a task before nightfall they would spoil it if they were not occupied with something else.

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿أَيُّوبَ﴾ — and there is substituted (badal) from it — ﴿إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ﴾ — when he was afflicted with the loss of all his wealth and children, the tearing of his body, and all people deserting him except his wife, for three years, or seven, or eighteen, and with the hardship of his living — ﴿أَنِّي﴾ — with fatḥa on the hamza, with the implied bāʾ — ﴿مَسَّنِيَ الضُّرُّ﴾ — i.e. hardship — ﴿وَأَنْتَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ﴾.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ — his call — ﴿فَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِ مِنْ ضُرٍّ وَآتَيْنَاهُ أَهْلَهُ﴾ — his children, male and female, in that they were brought back to life for him, each of the two kinds being three or seven — ﴿وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ﴾ — from his wife, whose youth was increased. He had a threshing floor for wheat and a threshing floor for barley, so Allah sent two clouds: one of them poured gold onto the wheat floor and the other poured silver onto the barley floor until it overflowed — ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ — a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose) — ﴿مِنْ عِنْدِنَا﴾ — an adjective (ṣifa) — ﴿وَذِكْرَى لِلْعَابِدِينَ﴾ — so that they may be patient and be rewarded.

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَإِدْرِيسَ وَذَا الْكِفْلِ كُلٌّ مِنَ الصَّابِرِينَ﴾ — in obedience to Allah and in refraining from disobeying Him.

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿وَأَدْخَلْنَاهُمْ فِي رَحْمَتِنَا﴾ — of prophethood. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ مِنَ الصَّالِحِينَ﴾ — for it. He was named Dhū al-Kifl because he took upon himself (takaffala) to fast all his days, to stand in prayer all his nights, and to judge between people without becoming angry; and he fulfilled that. And it is said that he was not a prophet.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿ذَا النُّونِ﴾ — the one of the fish, and he is Yūnus ibn Mattā; and there is substituted (badal) from it — ﴿إِذْ ذَهَبَ مُغَاضِبًا﴾ — with his people, i.e. angry with them for what he had endured from them, and he had not been given permission for that — ﴿فَظَنَّ أَنْ لَنْ نَقْدِرَ عَلَيْهِ﴾ — i.e. that We would not decree against him what We decreed, of confining him in the belly of the fish, or constrain him with that. ﴿فَنَادَى فِي الظُّلُمَاتِ﴾ — the darkness of the night, the darkness of the sea and the darkness of the fish's belly — ﴿أَنْ﴾ — i.e. "bi-an" (saying that) — ﴿لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ — in my leaving from among my people without permission.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ وَنَجَّيْنَاهُ مِنَ الْغَمِّ﴾ — by those words. ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ﴾ — just as We saved him — ﴿نُنْجِي الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ — from their distress, when they call on Us for help in supplication.

celaleyn:89-89.t: ﴿وَ﴾ — remember — ﴿زَكَرِيَّا﴾ — and there is substituted (badal) from it — ﴿إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ﴾ — by saying — ﴿رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْنِي فَرْدًا﴾ — i.e. without a child to inherit from me — ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ الْوَارِثِينَ﴾ — the One who remains after Your creation has perished.

celaleyn:90-90.t: ﴿فَاسْتَجَبْنَا لَهُ﴾ — his call — ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ يَحْيَى﴾ — as a son — ﴿وَأَصْلَحْنَا لَهُ زَوْجَهُ﴾ — so she bore the child after her barrenness. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ﴾ — i.e. the prophets mentioned — ﴿كَانُوا يُسَارِعُونَ﴾ — hastening — ﴿فِي الْخَيْرَاتِ﴾ — acts of obedience — ﴿وَيَدْعُونَنَا رَغَبًا﴾ — in Our mercy — ﴿وَرَهَبًا﴾ — of Our punishment — ﴿وَكَانُوا لَنَا خَاشِعِينَ﴾ — humble in their worship.
